> **Scope is the codex submodule** (`D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/`, a git submodule pointing at `gim-home/codex`). All code/workflow edits land inside that submodule, not the codexu repo root. The codexu repo only updates the gitlink + `plans/overview-data.js` after Part A merges.
>
> **No local cargo build is available** on this machine (per codexu CLAUDE.md "codex fork: no local cargo, CI is truth" and codex/CLAUDE.md "Build env is LLVM clang-cl + lld-link + xwin-staged Windows SDK"). All build verification happens on CI; the plan deliberately substitutes a `cargo metadata` parse for the bin-name probe and defers the workflow's correctness to a test tag push that runs `.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` end-to-end.

## Overview

The gim-home/codex fork ships codex via two paths — npm packages on GitHub Packages and a merged release tarball on GitHub Releases — both produced by `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`. The workflow currently builds and packages `codex.exe` + `codex-core.exe` + `rg.exe` but omits two binaries defined as bin targets of `windows-sandbox-rs`: `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` (consumed by the setup probe `find_setup_exe()` in `setup_orchestrator.rs:558-578`) and `codex-command-runner.exe` (consumed by the non-yolo elevated request path via `find_runner_exe()` in `elevated/runner_pipe.rs:43-44`, called from `elevated/runner_client.rs:231`). When users install codex from the published bundle and run it without `--yolo`, both gaps surface: codex-core fails to locate the setup binary, and the elevated request path fails to launch the missing runner. The fix is a single-file workflow edit with three touchpoints: add both bins to the `cargo build` invocation, add two vendor copies of the produced `.exe` files, and verify (no edit) that the release-bundle step's recursive `cp -R vendor` automatically carries the new files through. Part B produces a companion documentation file (`codex/docs/implementation/sandbox-setup-platform-matrix.md`) that inventories the per-platform sandbox-binary landscape, cites the upstream openai/codex release strategy, and writes the concrete delta the publish workflow would need if/when Linux + macOS distribution is added.

This plan splits into two stories. **Part A** is a workflow-only fix in a single file with a tag-push acceptance gate. **Part B** is a docs/research deliverable that produces the platform-matrix file plus an explicit bundling-vs-splitting recommendation. The two parts are independent in edit surface (different files, different review concerns) and can ship as one or two commits at the impl member's discretion, with the constraint that Part A's CI acceptance must pass before either lands on `gim-home/codex` `origin/main`.

### Technical Constraints

- **No local cargo build available.** Per codexu CLAUDE.md "codex fork: no local cargo, CI is truth" and codex/CLAUDE.md "Build env is LLVM clang-cl + lld-link + xwin-staged Windows SDK; the machine has Visual Studio but no VC++ C++ Tools". Local Rust verification is limited to `cargo metadata` (parses `Cargo.toml`, no compile). All compile-and-package verification defers to CI. The acceptance gate runs only when `publish-npm.yml` itself runs — that is, on a tag push.

- **CI is the only verifier, and the publish workflow has a strict tag-equals-version gate.** The `gim-home/codex` repo runs `.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml` on push to any branch (per codex/CLAUDE.md "Phase 5 invariant audits" and codexu CLAUDE.md "daily iter pushes to CI which runs invariant-check.yml"). The publish workflow `publish-npm.yml` runs only on `v*` tag push, and its first non-checkout step (`Read version from Cargo.toml and verify tag`, lines 32–46) hard-fails when `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` does not exactly equal `v${VERSION_CONTENT}`, where `VERSION_CONTENT` is parsed from `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` `workspace.package.version`. A suffixed test tag (e.g., `v0.X.Y-sandbox-test.1`) is therefore NOT viable — it will hit the gate and the workflow body (where the new bin builds + vendor copies live) will never run. Acceptance for US-001 must run against a real release tag whose value matches a Cargo.toml version bump. The fork's `/publish-sandbox-patch` skill (`codex/.claude/commands/publish-sandbox-patch.md`) is the authoritative path: it bumps the suffix in `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` via a submodule commit, commits the wrapper gitlink, then tags `v<NEW_VERSION>` (e.g., `v0.130.0-copilot-api.7`) and pushes. That tag is what `publish-npm.yml` runs against.

- **The fix is workflow-only.** No Rust source changes are required for Part A. No `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker, no `patch-surface.md §14` row, no `§15` rebase-replant note (those tenants apply to edits inside `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/`; the workflow file is wrapper-owned). The plan deliberately keeps Part A inside the wrapper-only surface to avoid any upstream-canonical conflict cost.

- **Part B is documentation-only.** The new doc lives under `codex/docs/implementation/` and joins the existing `architecture.md` + `patch-surface.md` neighbors. No engineering-tenant invariant changes; no test/guard required.

- **codex-command-runner.exe is also a runtime requirement on Windows.** Both `install.ps1` and `build_npm_package.py` already reference it, but the workflow does not build it. Source-code inspection of the non-yolo (elevated) code path confirms it is invoked from `codex-core` at runtime: `windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_pipe.rs:43-44` defines `find_runner_exe()` (calling `resolve_helper_for_launch(HelperExecutable::CommandRunner, ...)`), and `windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_client.rs:231` calls `find_runner_exe(...)` to launch the elevated runner. Both `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `codex-command-runner` are therefore in-scope for Part A; neither is optional.

## Approach

### Architecture

Two stories, both inside the codex submodule.

- **Story US-001 — Windows fix (Part A)**: edit `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` in three sites (one of which is a no-op verification). Bump `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` `workspace.package.version` via `/publish-sandbox-patch`, tag the corresponding `v<NEW_VERSION>` release on `gim-home/codex` (a suffixed test tag is non-viable — see Technical Constraints), observe `publish-npm.yml` produce a tarball containing the new binaries, smoke-test installation.

- **Story US-002 — Cross-platform investigation (Part B)**: create `codex/docs/implementation/sandbox-setup-platform-matrix.md` summarizing the per-platform sandbox-binary inventory, the upstream release model, the concrete delta vs current `publish-npm.yml` for Linux/macOS expansion, and a bundling-vs-splitting recommendation. Optionally — per the recommendation — file a follow-up task entry in `codexu/plans/overview-data.js`.

The stories touch disjoint files (workflow vs new doc) and can be implemented in either order. They are not dependent on each other. Story US-001's CI acceptance is on a separate clock from US-002 (US-002 needs no CI).

### Implementation Strategy

Recommended order, executed in the impl-phase ralph member:

1. **Verify bin target names** (one-time prereq for US-001). Run from `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/`:
    ```bash
    cargo metadata \
      --manifest-path external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml \
      --format-version 1 \
      | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.name | test("windows-sandbox")) | .targets[] | select(.kind | index("bin")) | .name'
    ```
   Expected output (one name per line): `codex-windows-sandbox-setup`, `codex-command-runner`. If either name differs, update Story US-001's edits to match.

2. **codex-command-runner is in-scope** (source-code citation; no decision step). Both `--bin codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `--bin codex-command-runner` ship in Part A. Justification: `windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_pipe.rs:43-44` defines `find_runner_exe()` calling `resolve_helper_for_launch(HelperExecutable::CommandRunner, ...)`, and `windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_client.rs:231` invokes it on the non-yolo (elevated) request path. Shipping only `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` would leave the elevated path broken with a missing `codex-command-runner.exe`.

3. **Story US-001 edits** to `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`:
   - Edit 1 (build step, lines 126–128): append `--bin codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `--bin codex-command-runner`.
   - Edit 2 (vendor copy, after line 138): insert `cp "$REL/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe" "$VENDOR/codex/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe"` and `cp "$REL/codex-command-runner.exe" "$VENDOR/codex/codex-command-runner.exe"`.
   - Edit 3 (release bundle, lines 224–248): **no edit**; verify by inspection that line 231's `cp -R "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/stage-platform/vendor" "$STAGE/vendor"` will carry the new files. Record the no-edit verification in the commit message.

4. **Update `codex/CLAUDE.md` Distribution string** to list the new binaries packaged. Short edit in the section that reads "It builds: codex.exe, codex-core.exe, rg.exe" — extend the list with `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` and `codex-command-runner.exe`.

5. **Bump the workspace version and tag a real release** via `/publish-sandbox-patch` (`codex/.claude/commands/publish-sandbox-patch.md`). This is mandatory, not optional: `publish-npm.yml` lines 32–46 enforce `TAG == "v${VERSION_CONTENT}"` against `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` `workspace.package.version`, so any suffix-only test tag (e.g., `v0.X.Y-sandbox-test.1`) fails before the build step runs. The fork's `/publish-sandbox-patch` skill is the authoritative version-bump path: it bumps the suffix (`NEW_VERSION="0.X.Y-copilot-api.<N+1>"`) inside the `external/repos/codex-patched` submodule via `sed -i 's/^version = ".*"$/version = "${NEW_VERSION}"/' external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml`, commits inside the submodule, commits the wrapper gitlink update, creates the `release/<NEW_VERSION>` retention tag on `codex-patched`, then tags `v${NEW_VERSION}` on `origin` (`gim-home/codex`) and pushes. Note: the verification therefore runs against the actual next release, not against a throwaway test tag. If the operator wants to avoid promoting an unverified-against-CI build to a real release in one shot, the alternative is to (a) bump `Cargo.toml` and the gitlink manually on a branch, (b) tag `v${NEW_VERSION}` from that branch, (c) let `publish-npm.yml` run and verify, (d) only then merge the branch to `main` — but the tag itself must still equal `v${NEW_VERSION}`. Wait for `publish-npm.yml` to complete on that tag.

6. **Verify CI artifacts** (acceptance for US-001):
   - Download the platform tarball (`codex-win32-x64` npm package or the GitHub Release bundle).
   - `tar tzf <bundle>.tgz | grep -E 'codex-(windows-sandbox-setup|command-runner)'` — expect both `vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/codex/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` and `vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/codex/codex-command-runner.exe`.
   - Run a clean install via `install.ps1`. Execute `codex exec "echo hello"` (no `--yolo`). Expect normal completion; specifically expect NO "cannot find sandbox-setup binary" error and NO "cannot find/launch codex-command-runner" error. The non-yolo path exercises both the setup probe and the elevated runner spawn (`find_runner_exe()` in `runner_pipe.rs:43-44`, invoked from `runner_client.rs:231`), so a clean completion is end-to-end evidence both bins are wired through.

7. **Story US-002 doc creation** in parallel (or after) US-001. Write `codex/docs/implementation/sandbox-setup-platform-matrix.md` with the four sections enumerated in Files to Create/Modify below.

8. **Decision step**: based on the doc's recommendation, optionally file `codex-cross-platform-publish` in `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/plans/overview-data.js`. This is a codexu-repo edit, not a codex-submodule edit — handle it separately by the bookkeeper after impl ships.

If selected, the impl-phase ralph member must explicitly justify it given Part A's small surface vs Linux/macOS expansion's large surface.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Workflow edit to `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` adding both `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `codex-command-runner` to the cargo build + vendor copy steps (Part A / Story US-001). Both bins are required: `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` is needed by the setup probe (`find_setup_exe()`) and `codex-command-runner` is needed by the non-yolo elevated path (`find_runner_exe()` at `runner_pipe.rs:43-44`, called from `runner_client.rs:231`).
- One-line documentation update in `codex/CLAUDE.md` § Distribution to keep the binary inventory accurate.
- Verification recipe: bin-name probe via `cargo metadata`, post-tag artifact inspection via `tar tzf`, post-install smoke test via `codex exec` without `--yolo`.
- Cut a real release tag `v<NEW_VERSION>` on `gim-home/codex` (driven by `/publish-sandbox-patch`, with the `Cargo.toml` workspace.package.version bumped to match) to exercise `publish-npm.yml`. A suffix-only test tag is not viable because of the `publish-npm.yml` lines 32–46 tag-vs-Cargo.toml gate.
- New docs file `codex/docs/implementation/sandbox-setup-platform-matrix.md` covering all four required sections (Part B / Story US-002).
- Either the file-a-follow-up-task action or an explicit bundle-it-now decision documented in the doc's "Recommendation" section.

### Out of Scope

- **Building, packaging, or publishing Linux or macOS binaries** in this PR. Part B *documents* the delta; it does not implement it.
- Rust source-code changes in `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/`. No `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker, no `patch-surface.md` invariant row, no rebase-replant note. The fix is workflow-only.
- Edits to `install.ps1`, `install.sh`, or `build_npm_package.py`. All three already reference the binary names correctly; verifying this is part of the plan, but editing them is not.
- Changes to `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot-launcher/`. The launcher discovers `codex-core` only; sandbox-setup discovery is delegated to `codex-core` at runtime and works correctly once the binary is in the install layout.
- Cleaning up old test-release tags in `gim-home/codex`. Leave them for the maintainer.
- Updating `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/plans/overview-data.js`. The impl-phase ralph member does **not** edit codexu state files; the bookkeeper handles that after the codex-submodule PR merges.
- Verifying *runtime* behavior of `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` itself (e.g., that it correctly installs Windows firewall rules / security tokens). Scope is "binary is now packaged and discovered"; broader behavioral testing is upstream of this task.

## Risk Areas

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Bin target name doesn't match `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` | Very low — confirmed by both research agents reading `windows-sandbox-rs/Cargo.toml:13-15` | Impl-phase step 1 re-verifies via `cargo metadata` before the edit. |
| Release bundle stage at lines 224–248 misses the new exe | Low — line 231 uses `cp -R`, a recursive whole-tree copy | Impl-phase step 6 (CI artifact inspection) checks `tar tzf` for the binary's presence in the bundle. |
| `find_setup_exe()` discovery probe doesn't match the install layout | Low — install.ps1 maps `vendor/codex/*.exe` → `codex-resources/*.exe`, and discovery probes `<exe-dir>/codex-resources/` second | Smoke test (step 6) is the end-to-end verifier. |
| **`codex-command-runner.exe` packaging gap (now in-scope)** | Resolved — both bins ship in Part A | Source-code citation (`runner_pipe.rs:43-44`, `runner_client.rs:231`) confirms runtime use on the non-yolo elevated path; no impl-phase decision required. Acceptance criterion #6 covers the elevated path via a non-yolo smoke test. |
| Verification requires cutting a real release (no throwaway test tag) | Medium | `publish-npm.yml` lines 32–46 hard-enforce `TAG == "v${VERSION_CONTENT}"`, so any suffix-only test tag fails the gate before the workflow body runs. Mitigation: drive the tag via `/publish-sandbox-patch`, which bumps `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` `workspace.package.version` in the same commit as the workflow edit so the tag matches. The acceptance verification therefore happens against the real release tag; pre-flight by reviewing the workflow diff carefully and (optionally) running CI on a feature branch first via `invariant-check.yml` to catch syntax issues before tagging. |
| LLVM/xwin build env on the windows-latest runner regresses | Very low — env is already wired up; the new bin compiles with the same toolchain as `codex-core.exe` | The cargo build step already exports `LIB`, `INCLUDE`, `CC`, `CXX`, `AR`, linker — no additional setup needed for the third bin. |
| Wrapper `codex/CLAUDE.md` Distribution string drifts again | Low — kept short, single bullet | Impl member adds the binary name; rebase-cadence drift is a separate concern outside this scope. |
| Recommendation in Part B ("Split" vs "Bundle") is contested by operator | Medium-low — recommendation is opinionated | Doc presents both options with reasons; final choice is reversible (Bundle can be reduced to Split at any time before the larger PR opens). |
| Part B doc lands without Part A — Distribution drift | Low | Recommend committing both stories together OR ensuring Part A lands first if split into two commits. Either ordering is acceptable; the constraint is only on the merge gate. |

## Acceptance Criteria

### Story US-001 — Windows fix

- [ ] `cargo metadata` (parsed Cargo.toml only, no compile) confirms bin target names are exactly `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `codex-command-runner`.
- [ ] `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` is edited as follows: `--bin codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `--bin codex-command-runner` appended to the `cargo build --release` invocation at lines 126–128; two new `cp` lines inserted after line 138 — `cp "$REL/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe" "$VENDOR/codex/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe"` and `cp "$REL/codex-command-runner.exe" "$VENDOR/codex/codex-command-runner.exe"`.
- [ ] `codex/CLAUDE.md` § Distribution lists both `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` and `codex-command-runner.exe` alongside `codex.exe`, `codex-core.exe`, `rg.exe`.
- [ ] `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` `workspace.package.version` is bumped to `<NEW_VERSION>` inside a submodule commit, and the wrapper gitlink is updated to that submodule SHA in a separate wrapper commit (the standard `/publish-sandbox-patch` shape). The release tag `v<NEW_VERSION>` is pushed to `gim-home/codex` (`origin`) and the `publish-npm.yml` run for that tag completes successfully (all steps green). The tag MUST exactly equal `v${VERSION_CONTENT}` parsed from Cargo.toml — `publish-npm.yml` lines 32–46 reject mismatches before the build step runs, so any suffix-only test tag is non-viable.
- [ ] `tar tzf` of the release-bundle tarball (downloaded from the GitHub Release for that tag) shows BOTH `vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/codex/codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` AND `vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/codex/codex-command-runner.exe`.
- [ ] Smoke test exercises BOTH the setup probe and the elevated (non-yolo) command-runner path on a **truly clean install**. Preconditions before the test: (a) on a Windows machine with NO prior `~/.codex-copilot/` directory and NO prior Windows Firewall rules from a previous codex install — use a fresh VM/sandbox, or delete those before testing so `find_setup_exe()` is actually invoked instead of short-circuiting on already-installed state; (b) authenticate via `codex login --provider copilot`. Then run the test in two passes: (1) **direct-disk presence check** — confirm both `<install-dir>\codex-resources\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` and `<install-dir>\codex-resources\codex-command-runner.exe` exist after `install.ps1` completes (this AC is hard, deterministic, and the primary verifier alongside the `tar tzf` check below); (2) **runtime path check** — run `codex exec "echo hello"` without `--yolo`, which exercises the non-yolo flow and invokes `find_runner_exe()` → `codex-command-runner.exe` for the elevated process. The command completes with exit code 0; no "cannot find sandbox-setup binary" error and no "cannot find/launch codex-command-runner" error appears in stderr or `~/.codex/log/`. Verify the runner actually spawned by inspecting `~/.codex/log/` for the elevated runner log entries.
- [ ] Final commit lands on `gim-home/codex` `main`. Because verification ran against the real release tag `v<NEW_VERSION>`, the merge to `main` is the same SHA that CI already validated.

## Open Questions

- **`codex-command-runner.exe` runtime use — resolved by source-code citation, not deferred.** `windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_pipe.rs:43-44` defines `find_runner_exe()` calling `resolve_helper_for_launch(HelperExecutable::CommandRunner, ...)`; `windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_client.rs:231` invokes it on the non-yolo (elevated) request path. Both `codex-windows-sandbox-setup` and `codex-command-runner` are in-scope for US-001; the impl member does NOT need to grep or decide. **Not an open question.**

- **Part B recommendation: "Split" vs "Bundle"?** Plan recommends **Split** based on Part A's urgency + Part B's larger surface, but final choice is the impl-phase ralph member's after writing the doc. If "Bundle" wins, the impl member must justify it in the doc and in the commit message. **No blocker — recommendation is reversible until either PR opens.**

- **Version-bump path is mandatory, not optional.** Resolved by source inspection of `publish-npm.yml` lines 32–46: the workflow's first non-checkout step enforces `TAG == "v${VERSION_CONTENT}"` against `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` `workspace.package.version` and exits non-zero on mismatch. A suffix-only test tag is therefore non-viable. The impl member drives the tag via the fork's `/publish-sandbox-patch` skill (`codex/.claude/commands/publish-sandbox-patch.md`), which bumps `Cargo.toml` inside the submodule, commits the wrapper gitlink update, and tags `v<NEW_VERSION>`. The verification consequently happens against the actual next release rather than a throwaway test tag; the acceptance flow in §Implementation Strategy step 5 and §Acceptance Criteria reflects this. **Not an open question.**
